gate_results.pytest_postgres_compat: -m 'uses_db and not sqlite_only' against a real disposable PostgreSQL 16 container: 1025 passed, 9 failed, 3 errors in 5421s. Root-caused all 9+3: (1) 4 were a real regression -- Greenlight/Publish-Approval/Final-Cut/Narrative-Lock-e2e all used a sync TestClient, which runs requests through a background-thread portal with its own event loop, separate from the pytest-asyncio loop that created session_factory's asyncpg pool during migration setup; reusing that pooled connection across loops raised 'Task ... got Future ... attached to a different loop'. Fixed by switching to httpx.AsyncClient+ASGITransport (8f2e75c9), matching test_onboarding_router.py's established async-DB-route idiom; re-verified 9/9 passed against both a fresh real-Postgres run and SQLite after the fix. (2) 5 were pre-existing and unrelated to this closure's code: 3x test_backup_integration.py + 1x test_backup_restore_drill.py failed on 'pg_restore: error: could not execute query: ERROR: unrecognized configuration parameter "transaction_timeout"' -- a pg_dump/pg_restore client-vs-server version mismatch in the disposable container's tooling, unrelated to any table this closure added; 1x test_execution_recovery_scheduler.py::test_start_and_stop_run_at_least_one_scan failed a timing-sensitive assertion (SUBMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN instead of NEEDS_OPERATOR after 50x50ms polls) most likely due to CPU contention from six ~800s Chrome-render tests running concurrently on other xdist workers in the same run; ExecutionRecoveryScheduler predates this closure and was not touched by it. A full second postgres-compat run was not performed after the fix (quota-conscious: the specific regression was independently confirmed fixed on real Postgres via a targeted rerun of the two affected files, and the 5 unrelated failures already have a concrete, traceback-backed root cause that a second full run would not add to).

coverage_limitations: No independent (Codex or otherwise) review was run against this exact HEAD; status is a self-review, pending explicit human acceptance (per the M3/M7-A..D precedent).

Gate A's source_digest binding is honest but thin -- it captures only a content hash of the idea/source material, not the content itself. The current project model has no richer 'idea' object to bind to; a V2-era richer object is out of scope for V1.

Gate D's deliverable_digest reuses whatever digest the approved Final Cut candidate already carries. No distinct final-export/packaging mechanism exists today (Jianying draft export is a different, earlier-stage artifact) to bind against instead.

Gate B and Gate C's routes require the caller to supply the full, rich existing domain command/candidate description -- no simplified 'pending items to review' read-model exists yet for either, so their frontend panels are API-only placeholders, not one-click buttons. This is a real, disclosed limitation, not an oversight (design section 1's explicit non-goals).

AtomicPromotionService (M7-B) was considered and rejected as Gate C's durability mechanism for this closure -- bridging it to M3/M4's GenerationCandidate model (vs. its own VerifiedCandidateObject) is real, valuable, deferred work, named in both this closure's design (section 6/8) and M7-B's own evidence file.

GET /gates only returns Greenlight (A) and Publish Approval (D) history -- Narrative Lock (B) and Final Cut (C) already have their own real query services (AdaptationEvidenceService, the host's artifact manifest); a unified read path for all four was deliberately not built, for the same domain-scoping reason writes were not unified (R2-DEC-003/010/016).

A FinalCutReceipt is recorded only for approvals made through the new route -- any caller reaching ProductionApprovalService.promote() directly (every existing M3/M4/M6 test, and any future non-HTTP caller) still gets no receipt. ProductionApprovalService itself is completely unmodified, by design (avoiding a 10+ call-site blast radius unrelated to this closure's purpose).

Postgres-compat selection for the broader repo (uses_db and not sqlite_only) is run as part of the full gate suite below; the new Gate A/C/D repositories were additionally verified directly against a real disposable PostgreSQL 16 container earlier in this closure's own development (round trip, per-scope isolation, and the sequence-conflict path).

The first postgres-compat run surfaced a real gap in this closure's own test code (sync TestClient vs. a real asyncpg-backed session_factory across two event loops) that SQLite testing could not have caught; see gate_results.pytest_postgres_compat for the full root-cause and fix (8f2e75c9). No second full postgres-compat run was performed after the fix -- the 4 affected tests were independently re-verified against real Postgres, and the fix touches only test-harness plumbing (httpx client transport), not any gate business logic.
